summary: Build practical cybersecurity skills for asset visibility, segmentation, monitoring, and incident response. Review the course and plan your training.
lede: Operational technology training covers practical ways to protect industrial control systems while accounting for operational constraints. It is for professionals who protect, operate, govern or report on these environments, and builds skills in mapping assets and network zones, reviewing remote access and traffic, and prioritizing risks and incident response. Exercises use simulated industrial data to create detection plans and management reports; advanced threat hunting and malware reverse engineering remain overview-level topics.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for protecting, operating, governing, or reporting on industrial control environments. It suits beginners to intermediate practitioners who understand their operational setting and need a structured OT cybersecurity method.
modules: OT Security Foundations and Purdue Architecture
OT Asset Visibility and Network Monitoring
OT Security Metrics and Executive Roadmaps
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop for reviewing simulated network captures, asset inventories, architecture diagrams, and digital templates. The course uses Wireshark and representative Zeek outputs for analysis exercises. No coding or software development is required, and lab materials can be supplied without installing tools on production networks.
